html:
A bank founded in Calcutta on 2 June 1806 as the Bank of Calcutta and renamed the Bank of Bengal in 1809. Through later mergers it became the State Bank of India, the country's largest bank.

It was set up mainly to fund the East India Company's government, whose costly wars against Tipu Sultan of Mysore and the Marathas had drained its treasury. It was a joint-stock bank with the government as a shareholder, and for decades it had the right to issue paper notes in its region.

Two sister banks followed, the Bank of Bombay in 1840 and the Bank of Madras in 1843. Together the three "presidency banks" were the main banks of British India. In 1921 they merged into the Imperial Bank of India, which acted partly as a central bank until the Reserve Bank of India took over that role in 1935. In 1955 independent India took control of the Imperial Bank and renamed it the State Bank of India.
sum: A bank founded in Calcutta on 2 June 1806 as the Bank of Calcutta and renamed the Bank of Bengal in 1809. Through later mergers it became the State Bank of India, the country's largest bank.
